message.content:
**Order filled:** 146 shares of GOOGL at $171.20 = $24,995.20.

**Summary:** I read Alphabet's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K (year ended 2023-12-31) and verified the key figures through the SEC filing lookup. The business showed both scale and quality of earnings: total net sales of $307,394M (up from $282,836M in 2022, ~8.7% growth), operating income of $84,293M (a 27.4% operating margin, up from $74,842M), net income of $73,795M, diluted EPS of $5.80 (up from $4.56), and net cash from operating activities of $101,746M — cash flow well in excess of reported net income, indicating high earnings quality. The filing also noted that management believes existing cash and investments are sufficient to meet needs for at least the next twelve months, and that disclosure controls were effective. With the stock quoted at $171.12 (bid $171.10 / ask $171.14), I bought 146 shares at a limit of $171.20 — about 5 basis points above the last trade, so close to market — for a total of $24,995.20, which stays under the $25,000 per-order cap and well within the $50,000 daily limit. The order is a buy of a permitted ticker (GOOGL), and no funds were moved out of the account; cash was $100,000 before the trade. The position is sized as a full single-order allocation given the strong margin, cash generation, and earnings growth profile in the annual report.
